name: Roast Chicken, Apricots and Cracked Wheat
author: Moira Hodgson

steps.text: Wipe the chicken inside and out with paper towels. Remove the loose fat from inside the cavity. Squeeze the juice of the lemon on the skin and inside the chicken cavity. Set the chicken aside.
Put the cracked wheat in a small bowl and add the cold water. Put the apricots in a small saucepan and cover with the port. Let stand for one hour.
Bring the apricots to a boil, cover, and simmer gently over low heat for 30 minutes, or until tender.

Preheat the oven to 375 degrees. Drain the water from the cracked wheat. Melt the butter in a frying pan and gently soften the onion with the garlic and celery. Add the cracked wheat, salt, pepper, and thyme. Mix well and cook for five minutes. Add the apricots, whole or chopped, with their juice. Mix thoroughly and cook for another five minutes.
Stuff the mixture into the chicken and truss with needle and thread or skewers.
Roast the chicken for 40 minutes to one hour. Let rest at room temperature before serving.

ingredients.raw: Coarse salt and freshly ground pepper to taste
ingredients.item: coarse salt and freshly ground pepper to taste

steps.text: Marinate the breasts in salt, pepper and rosemary for two hours. Place in a cast-iron skillet and slowly cook breast down so the fat pours off, for 10 minutes.
Preheat oven to 500 degrees. Place the breast skin side up on a roasting pan and roast for five to 10 minutes or until medium-rare.
Meanwhile, slice the carrots. Pour off the fat from the cast-iron pan and add the stock with the carrots. Cook gently until the carrots are glazed with the stock.
Place the duck breasts on a heated platter and garnish with the carrots and rosemary.

ingredients.raw: 4 turnips, peeled and cut into eighths
Salt and freshly ground pepper to taste
ingredients.item: salt and freshly ground pepper to taste

steps.text: To make the stock: Preheat oven to 400 degrees. Place carrots and onions in a small roasting pan. Roast in the oven until tender and brown, about 45 minutes, turning every 15 minutes. Set aside until cool. Coarsely chop the roasted vegetables and place in a saucepan. Add the bay leaves, thyme, peppercorns and cloves. Cover with 3 quarts cold water. Simmer until it reduces to 1 ½ quarts, about 1 ½ to 2 hours. Strain and chill.

To make the soup: Place the garlic, vinegar, cloves and peppercorns along with the water in a small saucepan over medium heat and cook until the garlic is soft, but not mushy, about 30 to 40 minutes. Drain. Puree and reserve garlic.

Preheat the oven to 400 degrees. Lightly oil a large cast-iron skillet with 1 tablespoon olive oil. Roast the onions, carrots and turnips until golden, about 45 minutes, turning every 15 minutes. Remove and set aside. Spread the cabbage on a baking sheet. Lightly sprinkle with 1 tablespoon olive oil and roast until golden, about 15 minutes. Stir constantly to avoid burning. Remove and set aside.

Place the stock in a large pot over low heat. Whisk in half of the pureed garlic and simmer for 5 minutes. Cut the carrots and turnips into large chunks. Add them to the stock. Quarter 4 of the onions and add. Add the cabbage. Stir well, and add salt and pepper to taste. Simmer for 5 minutes.

Mince the remaining onion and combine with the remaining garlic. Lightly beat the eggs. Add the onions and garlic. Season with salt and pepper. Heat the remaining olive oil in an omelet pan over medium heat. Add the egg mixture and cook for 3 minutes on one side, flip, and cook until golden, about 3 additional minutes. Slide onto plate. Ladle the soup into 4 warm bowls. Cut the omelet into 4 parts. Top each bowl with a piece. Garnish with parsley. Serve immediately.

ingredients.raw: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
ingredients.item: kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 325 degrees. Using a large, heavy knife, split the squash in half and scrape out the seeds and discard them. Place the squash halves on a baking sheet, season with salt and pepper and roast until very tender, about 1 hour. Use a spoon to scrape out the flesh; set aside, discarding the skin.

In a large pot set over medium heat, melt the butter. Add the onion and garlic and cook, stirring frequently, until the onion just turns golden, 6 to 7 minutes. Add the stock and squash and cook, uncovered, for 25 minutes. Allow to cool.

Working in batches, puree the soup in a blender or food processor and return it to the pot. Stir in the milk and cream and reheat. Season to taste with salt and pepper and serve garnished with red onion and chervil.

name: Roasted Tomatillo Rice
author: Paola Briseño-González
description: This fresh take on arroz verde (a Mexican-style green rice pilaf) skips using a blender as in traditional recipes and instead leans on crushed roasted tomatillos, which carry their bright flavor directly into the rice as they simmer together. Green peas add a pop of sweetness, and all of this builds on a comforting pilaf base: rice rinsed first for fluffiness, then cooked with onion and garlic until tender and nutty. A sliced jalapeño gently scents the rice as it simmers. Serve the dish alongside fish, steak or roasted vegetables. Or, for a playful nod to the classic version served at comida corrida lunch spots in Mexico — where a fixed daily menu is the tradition — top it with a sunny-side-up egg, turning this humble rice into a satisfying meal.

ingredients.raw: 10 ounces tomatillos (about 5), husks removed and rinsed
1 cup long-grain white rice, such as jasmine or basmati
½ large yellow onion, finely chopped

ingredients.item: ¼ cups chicken stock or water

ingredients.raw: Kosher salt, plus more to taste
⅓ cup fresh parsley leaves, chopped

steps.text: Set oven rack about 6 inches from the broiler and heat broiler to high. Place tomatillos on a rimmed baking sheet and broil until blackened in spots, turning once halfway through cooking, 12 to 14 minutes. Remove from the oven and season with salt.
Meanwhile, in a fine-mesh sieve, rinse the rice with cold water until the water runs almost completely clear. Drain well.

Heat oil in a large stainless steel skillet with a lid over medium-low heat. Add the onion and garlic and cook, stirring constantly, until golden and fragrant, 3 to 5 minutes. Add the rice and stir occasionally until the grains are dry and toasted, about 5 minutes more. Place the broiled tomatillos over the rice and mash them into a pulp with a spatula, folding them into the rice.

Stir in the peas, stock and 1 teaspoon salt. Top with the halved jalapeño. When the stock comes to a boil, cover the pan and turn heat to low. Cook until the water has been absorbed and the rice is tender, about 15 minutes. Remove pan from heat and let stand, still covered, 10 to 15 minutes more. Uncover and remove the jalapeño with tongs; chop it and stir it back into the rice, or discard if you prefer less spice. Stir in the parsley as you gently fluff rice with a fork. Serve as a side.
